definitions.explanation: A deep-fried breaded roll typically filled with mashed potato, ground meat, or cream. A staple of Japanese home cooking and street food.

examples.japanese: コロッケ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{揚|あ}げる→揚げる：16879_ageru⟧。
⟦{肉屋|にくや}→肉屋：15233_nikuya⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧コロッケ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{安|やす}くて→安い：00464_yasui⟧おいしい。
examples.english: The croquettes from the butcher shop are cheap and delicious.

examples.japanese: ⟦{母|はは}→母：00549_haha⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{手作|てづく}り→手作り：08300_tezukuri⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧コロッケ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}って→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧⟦くれた→くれる：00724_kureru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦{家族|かぞく}→家族：00552_kazoku⟧⟦みんな→みんな：02972_minna⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{食|た}べた→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
examples.english: My mother made homemade croquettes for us, so the whole family ate them together.

notes:
コロッケ comes from French "croquette" and is a very popular dish in Japan, available at supermarkets, butcher shops, and as street food.

COMMON VARIETIES:
- ⟦ポテト→ポテト：11170_poteto⟧コロッケ: potato croquette (the most common type)
- ⟦クリーム→クリーム：00253_kuriimu⟧コロッケ: cream croquette (filled with béchamel sauce)
- カニクリームコロッケ: crab cream croquette
- カボチャコロッケ: pumpkin croquette
- ⟦メンチカツ→メンチカツ：15300_menchikatsu⟧: minced meat cutlet (related but distinct)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- コロッケ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{揚|あ}げる→揚げる：16879_ageru⟧: to deep-fry croquettes
- コロッケ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}る→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧: to make croquettes
- ⟦{揚|あ}げたて→揚げたて：16736_agetate⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧コロッケ: freshly fried croquettes

CULTURAL NOTE:
コロッケ is considered a classic ⟦{惣菜|そうざい}→惣菜：05827_souzai⟧ (prepared side dish) and ⟦{庶民|しょみん}→庶民：12427_shomin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{味|あじ}→味：00826_aji⟧ (comfort food of ordinary people). Buying hot croquettes from a ⟦{肉屋|にくや}→肉屋：15233_nikuya⟧ (butcher shop) is a nostalgic experience for many Japanese people.
